title: Diameter-Ramsey triangles below the $135^\circ$
summary: A finite Euclidean set is diameter-Ramsey if, for every number of colors, some finite same-diameter witness has the property that every coloring of the witness contains a monochromatic congruent copy of the set. Frankl, Pach, Reiher and Rödl asked whether any obtuse triangle is diameter-Ramsey. We prove the stronger statement that every non-degenerate triangle whose largest angle is strictly smaller than $135^\circ$ is diameter-Ramsey.
